A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UAE/Unified-GRPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite section relocation and pagination changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original UAE experiments on generation, understanding, and Unified-Bench, alongside architecture ablations, training dynamics, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds a larger Unified-Bench evaluation and an OCR/document-understanding decoder comparison in Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: v5 introduces an auxiliary model variant replacing SD3 with Qwen-Image as the decoder for the OCR/DU experiment (Table 11). This changes a component for that variant; the core reconstruction pipeline, CLIP reward, GRPO procedure, and original UniWorld/Janus-Pro implementations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The documented training data and evaluated tasks remain the same. The 2,000-image experiment enlarges Unified-Bench rather than introducing a distinct task or domain, and OCR/DU were already evaluated within MMT-Bench.

E2.justification: The added scaled Unified-Bench comparison uses BAGEL and GPT-Image*, a narrower comparator panel than the original Table 2. GPT-Image* is described as the latest version, without an exact release identifier. The original comparator sets in Tables 1–9 remain intact.

E3.justification: v5 adds a 2,000-source-image Unified-Bench evaluation alongside the retained 100-image evaluation, a substantial twentyfold expansion of this central benchmark's test size. It also adds an SD3-versus-Qwen-Image decoder experiment for OCR/DU. Existing evaluation metrics and documented training hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 11 adds a targeted decoder ablation testing whether the OCR/DU degradation arises from the generator's text-rendering capability. Existing architecture ablations, ViT-freezing evidence, training curves, and case studies are retained. The new MSE discussion supplies rationale, not an empirical reward ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new tables continue reporting point estimates. Enlarging the evaluation sample does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain identical results. New Table 10 reports 2,000-image averages of 84.74 for UAE, 83.69 for GPT-Image*, and 80.95 for BAGEL. Table 11 adds Qwen-Image decoder results of 75.9 OCR and 70.5 DU, alongside encoder-only 75.0/70.0 and SD3 68.8/58.4. These are additional experimental settings, not same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: v5 removes v4 Section 2.1's explicit normalized-advantage definition and GRPO objective, including the clipped surrogate and KL term in Equations (1)–(2), substituting a citation. The retained probability-ratio and reconstruction-reward expressions are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: the auto-encoder perspective, reconstructive Unified-GRPO, mutual understanding/generation benefits, and Unified-Bench. The rewritten conclusion reiterates these claims; the additional experiments do not redefine their central scope.

C2.justification: v4 conjectures that decoder text-rendering weaknesses cause OCR/DU losses. v5 strengthens that interpretation using the decoder substitution experiment. It also explains why semantic CLIP rewards suit the text bottleneck better than pixel MSE and identifies long-instruction handling as an applicability requirement, including possible short-token-limit bottlenecks.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly identifies SD3 as the decoder underlying the OCR/DU analysis and names its Qwen-Image replacement. It removes the reproducibility statement promising public release of data, benchmark, code, weights, and configurations upon publication. Existing training settings and prompts remain; the deletion does not establish that previously available resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: v5 adds three cited works: Visual Lexicon, Reconstruction Alignment Improves Unified Multimodal Models, and Towards Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrail. It explicitly acknowledges related reconstruction-based post-training. Most architectural related-work discussion is relocated from the appendix to main Section 4 rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: v5 removes the GRPO background subsection, moves architectural related work into the main text and limitations into the appendix, rewrites the conclusion, and removes the LLM-use and reproducibility statements. It also makes localized wording and footnote edits. Most exposition remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 10–11 and reflows existing displays, including moving Table 3 between columns and relocating appendix figures relative to the prose. Figures 1–14 and the content and structure of Tables 1–9 are retained; there is no substantial graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: The larger Unified-Bench evaluation strengthens empirical support, while Table 11 supplies evidence for v4's previously conjectural decoder explanation of OCR/DU degradation. The reward and applicability discussions also improve clarity. These gains outweigh limited losses in self-contained documentation from removing the GRPO equations and resource-release statement, but sparse details for the added experiments and unchanged main results limit the overall improvement.
